name: Old Babylonian square-diagonal calculation
summary: A Babylonian school-style tablet shows a square with its diagonal and a sexagesimal value for the square root of two accurate to about six decimal places.
description: A square-diagonal calculation expressed in sexagesimal notation, represented by the inscribed approximation and product on YBC 7289.
tier_reason: Retain2 for this diagram/tablet witness. Being the strongest surviving witness is expressly not an impact reason for promotion. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: 19th–17th century BCE (Old Babylonian)
date.basis: The institutional catalogue dates the tablet to the Old Babylonian period, with uncertain southern Mesopotamian origin.

events.statement: A scribe wrote a square diagram with a numerical diagonal and an approximation to the square root of two.
events.caveats: Whether the scribe calculated the numbers independently or copied a worked example is not established; southern Mesopotamian origin is tentative.

evidence.supports: The square diagram includes a numerical square-root-of-two approximation and corresponding diagonal value.
